_about: Episode 1 outline, beat level.  The Fountain script (ep1/script.fountain) will be written from this; each beat becomes a [[beat: id]] note there.
'gist' is a sketch of what is said, not final dialogue.  'lines' fills with stable line IDs once the script exists.
Every number here is claimed against math_objects.json; run check_outline.py after any change.
title: The Curious Game of Twenty-One

scenes._comment: Series main title, then this episode's subtitle; see titles/outline.json.
scenes.subtitle: sub.ep1

beats.purpose: Pascal announces blackjack; the others expect the casino game
beats.gist: PASCAL: Blackjack! Twenty-one! SOPHIE: Where are the kings? ADA: There are twelve cards, zero to eleven. I counted.

beats.purpose: Six cards face up form one hand both players share; six go to the pile
beats.gist: PASCAL: One hand, face up, and we both play it. The rest is the pile.

beats.purpose: A move swaps one hand card for a smaller pile card; the total goes down
beats.gist: PASCAL: Give the hand a card, take a smaller one from the pile. Down, never up.

beats.purpose: The new total must stay at 21 or more; Pascal tries 11 for 1 and Ada stops him
beats.gist: PASCAL swaps eleven for one. ADA: Twenty. Below twenty-one. Put it back.

beats.purpose: If you have no legal move, you lose; totals only fall, so every game ends
beats.gist: ADA: And if you can't move? PASCAL: You lose. ADA: Then the game has to end. The total only goes down.

beats.purpose: Pascal plays first from the hand totaling 30; viewers are asked to choose a move
beats.gist: PASCAL (to camera): Fourteen legal moves. Which would you play?

beats.purpose: Pascal plays 7 for 5, with swagger; total 28
beats.gist: PASCAL: Seven out, five in. Twenty-eight. Your move.

beats.purpose: Ada plays 11 for 7; total 24
beats.gist: ADA thinks, then trades eleven for seven. Twenty-four.

beats.purpose: Pascal plays 6 for 3; total 21 and Ada has no legal move
beats.gist: Six out, three in: twenty-one. ADA looks for a smaller card that keeps twenty-one. There isn't one. PASCAL wins.

beats.purpose: Euler asks whether that was skill or luck; Ada demands proof
beats.gist: EULER: Was that skill, or luck? PASCAL: Skill. Obviously. ADA: Prove it.

scenes.title: The dead hand and its shadow

beats.purpose: Sophie deals 1 to 6: total 21, no moves, the player to move loses at once
beats.gist: SOPHIE: One, two, three, four, five, six. Twenty-one. PASCAL: Twenty-one again. Whoever moves first just loses.

beats.purpose: Euler swaps hand and pile: the complement totals 45 and has thirty legal moves
beats.gist: EULER: What about the other six? The complement. Forty-five.

beats.purpose: Pascal grabs the 45-hand and moves first; Ada answers each try and he loses every time
beats.gist: PASCAL: Thirty moves! This one's mine. Ten for one. ADA: Seven for three. (Montage: Pascal tries again and again; each game ends with him stuck.)
beats._cue_note: The montage must be played out by the game engine from these two openings, with Ada always replying into a hexad; do not hand-animate it.

beats.purpose: Ada notes they tried a few of thirty moves; Sophie poses the mystery
beats.gist: ADA: We tried a handful of thirty. That's an experiment. SOPHIE: Twenty-one loses. Forty-five loses. Why would those two be the same?

beats.purpose: Pascal guesses that only totals 21 and 45 lose; Euler calls it a conjecture

conjectures.text: Only the totals 21 and 45 lose; every total in between wins

beats.gist: PASCAL: Simple. Twenty-one and forty-five are the bad totals. Anything in between, I win. EULER: That's a conjecture.

beats.purpose: Ada deals a hand totaling 24 and lets Pascal move; it has only five legal moves
beats.gist: ADA: Twenty-four. In between. Your move.

beats.purpose: All five moves fan out as branches; each has a reply that lands on exactly 21. Checking every move is a proof, for this one hand
establishes: The hand {0,1,2,4,7,10} is a losing position
beats.gist: Each branch: PASCAL moves, ADA replies, twenty-one, stuck. ADA: Every hand you leave me is a winning position: I can reach twenty-one. Five moves, five answers. I checked them all. That's not luck. It's a proof, for this hand.

beats.purpose: Sophie lines up the losing hands so far; the 45-hand gets a question mark because it was only tested
beats.gist: SOPHIE: These lose. This one probably loses. They look special. But special how?

beats.purpose: Euler wonders whether Pascal's 28 after 7 for 5 was one of them

conjectures.text: The hand Pascal left at 28 is one of the special ones

beats.gist: EULER: Pascal, the hand you gave Ada at twenty-eight. Was it one of these? PASCAL: ...Naturally.

beats.purpose: Sophie decides the special hands need a picture (the bridge to Episode 2)
beats.gist: SOPHIE: I think I need to draw this. ADA: Draw a card game? SOPHIE: Draw what it's hiding.

scenes._comment: End-credits screenplay (end_credits/outline.json), then the next_time tail.
